message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: Deploy
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: Void
        default: v0
        required: false
jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      deployments: write
    name: Deploy
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 24.18.0
          cache: 'npm'
      - name: Build
        run: npm install && npm run build:all
        env:
          CI: false
      - name: Publish Genshin Music Nightly
        uses: cloudflare/wrangler-action@v3
        with:
          apiToken: ${{ secrets.CF_PAGES_TOKEN }}
          accountId: ${{ secrets.CF_ACCOUNT_ID }}
          command: pages deploy ./build/genshinMusic --project-name=genshin-music-nightly
      - name: Publish Sky Music Nightly
        uses: cloudflare/wrangler-action@v3
        with:
          apiToken: ${{ secrets.CF_PAGES_TOKEN }}
          accountId: ${{ secrets.CF_ACCOUNT_ID }}
          command: pages deploy ./build/skyMusic --project-name=sky-music-nightly",
  "rationale": "The P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT pattern (bound jobs with a custom timeout) is supported by measured experiment evidence (experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508) showing adding timeout-minutes: 5 to a CI job reduced median elapsed time by ~26.8% while all runs still succeeded. The repository's own CI history shows successful deploy runs completing in about 1-2 minutes, so a 5-minute bound provides headroom without interrupting valid runs. The change is minimal (one job-level key), preserves every build/publish step, all permissions, and required-check coverage, and adds no new network access, secrets, or privileged actions.",
  "evidence_ids": ["experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508"]
}
